column32: Raag Basant/Vasant raagmala. Pakhawj seems to have a symmetrical design. In today's pakhawaj, it is oblique. The belly is slightly towards the Dhuma, the base head.

Tabla is visible here. Dagga (Bayan) does not have shyai. Tuning patch. 20 Female dancers. One Sarangiya is lefty.

We are ambiguous about whether the  person ahead of everyone is a singer (In that case he is holding Tanpura) or a Satariya (In that case he is holding a Sitar). If he is a Sitariya, why is he sitting ahead is a question. If he is a singer, then the instrument in his hand has frets so it can not be Tambur. In all,

Assuming that he is a Sitar player who is tuning the sitar because the instrument has frets. And tuning because every one else is involved in the activity. He is the only one not playing.

1. There are 2 Tabla players.
2. Both Tabla and Dagga has shyai.
3. Tabla seems accompanying singers and dancers, played standing.
4. Lady seems to be the lead singer for Tabla accompaniment.
5. Pakhawaj and Rabab men are sitting in less busy corner.
6. Pakhawaj Bayan also has shyai.
7. Pakhawaj is with Tambora and Rabab. One person is sitting probably indicating taal or singing not sure.
8. Rabab and Tambora seems not played. Are they listening to Pakhawajiya?
9. They seem to have their parallel music. Does not look like they are playing for the main celebration with dance. They are engrossed within their own group of 4


Painting combines multiple views. King is seen on all the three floors. Lower floor has depictions of Sex positions but I did not see Dashavtar as noted by the museum. Though there are some sketches of gods

1. Both Sitar and Been.
2. Sitar playing women's position seems non sitar. She is using it as a Tanpura, but it has frets that indicates that it is a Sitar.
3. Presence of singer is indeterminate. The person sitting ahead of everyone is whether dancing or singing is difficult to understand. Though probably sitariya is singing.
4. Pakhawajiya is probably left handed. Left head has shyai. Right head seems to be the base drum. No ata visible.
5. Wooden pegs on both the sides.
7. Explicit dance performance.
Drinking scene. Whether the queen is offering drink or drinking herself is indetermiinate

1. No frets visible on the lute. So it is Tanpura. Also 4 tuning pegs are visible like the tanpura of today.
2. The barrel drum is indeterminate. It can not be Dholak because the right hand has Shyai. It cant be pakhawaj because both heads are of the same size.
3. Important detail is that the left hand does not show the shyahi as all black it is just a circle. Indicator of Ata?
4. The person at back is doing something in mouth. Is it a Morchang?

Quet an unusual collection of musicians and instruments. Though finely detailed. Lips of the Morchang and Tambura player are open indicating some activity through lips. Percussionist is mum.
Child is playing with some toys, miniature Horses and elephants.

And a toy, elephant killing tiger. :)
